record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
record.original_question: For an n-dimensional toric Gorenstein singularity with associated polytope Delta_{n-1}, minimized Sasaki-Einstein volume V_{n,min}, Euler number chi of a complete resolution, and first Chern class c_1, Conjecture 3.1 proposes bounds 1/chi <= V_{n,min} < m_n \int c_1^{n-1}. Can one prove or disprove this conjecture, determine the correct optimal bounds if needed, and explain the relation between equation (3.1) and the polygon-area bound in equation (3.2), especially their upper bounds?

evidence.quote: Question 13. Prove or disprove Conjecture 3.1. If the conjecture is true, are these the best bounds? If the conjecture is not true, find the correct bounds. Also, can we find the connections between (3.1) and (3.2) (in particular for their upper bounds)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be an n-dimensional toric Gorenstein singularity, realized as the affine toric Calabi–Yau cone over a Sasaki–Einstein base, and let Δ_{n−1} denote its associated (n−1)-dimensional toric diagram (a lattice polytope encoding the toric data). Let V_{n,min} denote the minimized volume of the Sasaki–Einstein base, obtained by Z-minimization (equivalently, volume minimization over the Reeb cone). Fix a complete (crepant) toric resolution Y → X and let χ(Y) denote its Euler number and c_1 = c_1(Y) its first Chern class; set ∫ c_1^{n−1} for the integral of the (n−1)-st power of c_1 over the appropriate compact cycle of Y. Finally let m_n be the explicit dimension-dependent constant.

(a) Prove or disprove the conjectured bounds
    1/χ(Y) ≤ V_{n,min} < m_n · ∫ c_1^{n−1}.
(b) If the conjecture holds, determine whether these are the optimal (sharpest) lower and upper bounds; if it fails, find the correct optimal bounds.
(c) In the two-dimensional toric (reflexive polygon) case, an alternative bound is given in terms of the lattice area A(Δ) of the associated polygon. Establish the precise relationship between the polytope-volume/Euler-number bound and the polygon-area bound, particularly comparing their upper-bound forms.
artifact.category_tag: Sasaki-Einstein volumes of toric Calabi-Yau cones
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., a 2024 study of Futaki invariants and reflexive polygons) continues to test and refine such volume bounds for toric Calabi–Yau cones using reflexive polytope data, without announcing a proof or disproof of the conjectured bounds 1/χ ≤ V_{n,min} < m_n ∫ c_1^{n−1}. No source found establishes optimality nor clarifies the connection between the two upper bounds, so the conjecture appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Futaki Invariants and Reflexive Polygons
status_evidence.snippet: Volumes of Sasaki–Einstein base and bounds in terms of topological quantities of toric varieties from reflexive polytopes are investigated.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent investigations continue to study and conjecture bounds on Sasaki–Einstein volumes via reflexive polytope data without resolving the conjectured bounds.

status_evidence.title: Calabi-Yau Volumes and Reflexive Polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Minimized volumes of Sasaki–Einstein bases are computed and bounds in terms of Euler number and Chern classes are conjectured for reflexive polytopes up to dimension 4.
status_evidence.claim: The bounds in question were proposed via reflexive-polytope data; no full proof or disproof is reported.
